item.title: Q: Testing for Measurement Invariance (MI)
item.description:
Hi! So I’m ultimately trying to run a cross-lagged panel model and am checking for measurement invariance first to ensure I at least have metric fit. However, when I put all my variables into one model, it will not converge (or at least is taking 20hours and it still running. Side note: I’m using lavaan in R and have a very old computer).
So my question is: can I test for MI in separate “models”? In other words, for my CLPM, I will be running 6 separate models: 1. Predictor —> mediator 1 —> outcome 1 2. Predictor —> mediator 2 —> outcome 1 3. Predictor —> mediator 3 —> outcome 1 4. Predictor —> mediator 1—> outcome 2 5. Predictor —> mediator 2 —> outcome 2 6. Predictor —> mediator 3 —> outcome 2
I don’t actually specify any paths when testing for MI, but is there a problem with running them separately, including only the variables relevant in each model? This is what I began doing initially, and the models were converging fine. I appreciate any input !!
